newsitem.title: CHINA: HSBC hits high on earnings hopes.
newsitem.headline: HSBC hits high on earnings hopes.

text.p: Shares of HSBC Holdings Plc hit a high on overseas buying, supported by strong earnings hopes ahead of the release of the bank's interim results due on August 4, brokers said on Monday.
"Anticipation of a strong earnings report plus excitement from the Liu Chong Hing Bank deal aided buying for HSBC," said Sean Li, associate director at Amsteel Securities.
HSBC rose HK$4.00 to HK$249 at midday after hitting an all-time high of HK$250. Volume was 1.89 million shares worth HK$467.8 million.
"As an international bank, HSBC looks relatively cheap following the rise of other banks such as Hang Seng Bank and Bank of East Asia," Li added.
HSBC was trading at a 16.8 times price to earnings (P/E) multiple while its subsidiary Hang Seng Bank was trading at 25.6 times P/E and Bank of East Asia was at 22.6 times P/E.
Last week, COSCO Pacific Ltd had proposed to buy 89 million shares or 20 percent of Liu Chong Hing Bank's enlarged share capital.
The move had fueled hopes of possible China participation in other smaller banks and helped drive demand for bank stocks generally.
